decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach with both arms separated. Plan cars in white, cameras in blue, watches in red; geometry will be refined from wrist views.
Approach left wooden car and rightmost camera from above, gradually rotating grippers across their widths. Keep clearance while establishing top-down grasps.
Finish vertical gripper orientation and descend cautiously over the first car and far-right camera. Open jaws; check alignment before closing.
Wrist images show both targets off-center. Correct toward the objects and lower slightly, retaining open jaws for another visual check.
Close left jaws on the centered car and test a small lift. The right camera shifted during descent; raise and realign rather than assuming a grasp.
Lift the left car clear toward white basket. Center the right camera deeper between the jaws, descend, and close for a retention test.
Car visibly retained; move fully over white basket and open. Lift the grasped right camera before carrying it inward toward the blue basket.
Left forward reach was interrupted; car already appears over white interior. Open here, then retreat toward second car. Carry right camera inward at clearance height, staying right of center.
First car visible inside white. Align left jaws with the second car and descend to pregrasp. Bring retained camera over the right side of blue, lowering to avoid the forward reach limit.
Right near forward reach limit: tilt fingers forward over blue instead of extending the EE farther. Fine-align and lower left over the second car; inspect both before release or closure.
Release right camera over blue and withdraw toward the next camera. Correct left car centering using wrist view, then close; retention remains to be tested.
Test second-car retention by lifting, then carry left toward white. Reorient right gripper across the middle camera's narrow width at safe height.
Second car was not retained. Return open and center lower over it. Right wrist shows camera farther forward than estimated; correct forward while descending with jaws open.
Use wrist centering: shift left along the car toward its body and lower; right camera is nearly centered. Close both and perform a small lift to test retention.
Both targets are now between closed jaws. Lift clear first, then carry car toward white and camera toward blue; tilt slightly forward to reduce reach demand.
Left car slipped during lift; return for a deeper body grasp, keeping forward tilt. Carry retained right camera farther inside blue before opening.
Release camera inside blue. Left approach contacted the off-center car; lift clear, restore vertical orientation and shift across its body before descending again. Right withdraws toward watches.
Reapproach car vertically at a lower body-grasp height, avoiding forward-tilt offset. Bring right gripper vertically over the black watch; inspect alignment before closing.
Fine-center left car between jaws and close at body height. Lower right slightly onto the centered watch, close, and test both with a short vertical lift.
Car and watch moved with jaws during test lift. Lift clear and carry toward white and red respectively, maintaining closure and introducing only a small forward tilt.
Advance the retained car fully inside white, lower and release. Continue carrying the watch over red with clearance from the front rim; keep right jaws closed until placement is verified.
Both cars are inside white. Release watch inside red, then withdraw toward silver watch. Move left toward the remaining camera while reorienting across its width.
Center remaining camera and silver watch from wrist views. Rotate left across camera width while descending; keep both jaws open until low alignment is checked.
Fine-center camera laterally and lower both to grasp height. Close on the remaining camera and silver watch, then make a short lift to verify retention from RGB.
Camera is retained; lift and carry toward blue. Silver watch shifted out of the right jaws, so open and clear the right arm while the left completes its central placement.
Carry the last camera over the left interior of blue, lowering and tilting forward modestly. Hold right clear until the camera placement is verified.
Release last camera over blue and withdraw left to clear the center. Reposition right at the centerline for the remaining silver watch, without crossing the arms.
Camera released inside blue. Withdraw left and begin returning its orientation. Rotate right to pinch the silver watch's near-right band segment while keeping the EE in the right workspace.
Continue left return at safe clearance. Descend right toward the silver watch's near-side band, finishing the cross-band orientation and small lateral centering correction.
Lower onto the silver watch band, close, and test a short lift. Return the empty left arm toward its original pose with continuous small orientation increments.
Test whether the silver watch is retained by lifting farther before carrying rightward. Keep right jaws closed; make a small final correction to the left origin pose.
Silver watch remains on the table. Reopen and reapproach its centerline band with a slight inward gripper tilt, keeping the right EE on its own side and the left at origin.
Use wrist view to center the watch ring across the open jaws while lowering slowly. Keep inward tilt fixed and verify the band alignment before another closure.
The watch ring is now centered between the open jaws. Close without translation, then test a short vertical lift before any transport.
The lift did not retain the watch. Reopen and bring the ring deeper into the jaw contact region, using a slower, lower approach rather than transporting an empty grasp.
The watch now sits deeper between the jaw contact surfaces. Close in place and lift vertically to check retention before moving toward red.
Empty closure suggests the jaws missed the band. Reopen and target the solid watch face nearer the table, shifting slightly inward and toward the face while lowering cautiously.
At lower height the watch spans the jaw contact area. Relieve slight table contact, center laterally, then close and test another small lift without transporting.
Watch appears caught between both jaws after the lower grasp. Lift clear first, then begin a gentle rightward carry while checking retention from RGB.
Silver watch is visibly retained above the table. Carry it across the right workspace toward red, introducing a gentle forward tilt while keeping jaws closed.
Move silver watch farther inside red away from the front rim, lower gently, then open and allow it to settle beside the black watch.
Both watches are visible inside red. Withdraw the empty right gripper upward and backward, returning its orientation gradually; make a small left-origin correction.
Continue the empty right arm toward origin with gradual orientation recovery and elbow-up continuity. All visible objects remain grouped in their baskets.
